title: Midway in life
hookLine: the middle of the road, as Dante's Comedy begins: a dark wood, a sunlit hill, and a guide already sent
tomorrow: her sons begged her to stay. why did the queen walk into the forest?

lines: A DARK WOOD, THE WAY LOST.
A HILL WITH THE SUN ON IT.
cards: It can arrive in the middle of an ordinary week: a commute, a meeting, and the sudden thought, how did I get here? Dante put that moment in the first line of his Comedy. In Italian: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita.
Midway along the journey of our life, he says, I found myself in a dark wood, the straight way lost. Ahead is a hill with the sun on its shoulders. He starts to climb.
Three beasts block the road: a leopard, a lion, a she-wolf. She drives him back down, to the place where, he says, the sun is silent.

teach.b: Then someone appears in the gloom: the ghost of Virgil, the old Roman poet. He has come to guide Dante the long way round, down through hell and up the mountain, because the short climb is closed. Why him, and why now?
In the next canto Virgil explains. A lady in heaven, whom tradition takes to be Mary, saw Dante's trouble. She called Lucy.
Lucy went to Beatrice, the woman Dante had loved, and Beatrice came down and sent Virgil. She gives her reason in one line: love moved me. The help was on its way before Dante asked for it.

That's a Catholic teaching, told as a story: grace comes first. In Catholic teaching, God's help goes ahead of us, and even the first step toward God is already a gift. Dante can't reach the sunny hill by trying harder.

teach.h: THE LONG WAY, WITH A GUIDE.
teach.b: He needs a guide, and a longer road.
The way out of the wood goes down before it goes up. So the middle of life, in this poem, isn't a crisis to hide.
It's the place where you finally notice the wood, the light and the beasts, and let someone walk you through.

how: Dante's Comedy opens midway along life's road, in a dark wood. Catholic teaching holds that grace goes before us: the poem shows it as help sent from heaven, through a lady tradition identifies as Mary, Lucy and Beatrice, before Dante asks.

o: the exact age a midlife crisis is supposed to start
the middle of life's road, where Dante finds himself lost
the halfway point of a long hike up a mountain

drives him back down the hill

s: Dante's Comedy opens with him already in hell
it opens midway along life's road, lost in a dark wood, before any descent.
in the poem, help is sent before Dante asks for it
a lady in heaven, Lucy and Beatrice set it in motion; Virgil explains it in canto 2.
Dante escapes the wood by climbing straight up the sunlit hill
the beasts drive him back; he has to take the long road, with a guide.

games.q: a friend says she'll fix her stuck middle-of-life alone, by willpower, starting monday. what does Dante's opening suggest?
o: he couldn't climb the bright hill alone; a guide came, and the road was longer.
willpower is enough: Dante sprinted up the hill and never looked back.
nothing helps midway; the poem says to stay in the wood and wait.
games.why: the she-wolf drives Dante back down. Virgil, sent by Beatrice, takes him the long way round. In the poem, grace goes first.

practice: Find the brightest thing in the room: a window, a lamp, a patch of sun on the floor. Rest your eyes on it softly for a few breaths, the way Dante looked up at the hill.
Then close your eyes and ask, in this middle of your life: what's lit, and what's dark wood?

wordCard.voice: Midway in life: Dante's middle of the road, where he finds himself lost, and where help is already on its way, sent by love.

orig.note: Italian, written in the Latin alphabet: the dark wood of the Comedy's opening lines.

carryVoice: The line for the road: midway, the dark wood and the guide already sent before he asked. Day 1684, in the middle of the road.
